title: The frontend shows a breadcrumb trail above the back link on 34 screens and an empty one on the dashboard; DR1 uses no breadcrumbs anywhere.

finding.frontend: 37 of the 40 captured screens render a breadcrumb trail — "Your notifications" then the page name — from `src/server/app/shared/layout.njk:42-48`. On 34 of them it sits directly above a "Back" link, so the page offers a user two competing ways back at the same time. The three task-list screens are the only ones that suppress it. On both dashboard captures the trail renders as an empty navigation landmark: a navigation region labelled "Breadcrumb" containing a list with no items in it at all, which a screen reader announces as a navigation region a user can enter and find nothing in.
finding.prototype: No DR1 screen shows breadcrumbs, and no view in the prototype references the component. Every DR1 page that needs a way back offers the back link alone, directly under the phase banner — `app/views/declaration.html:21-24`.
finding.difference: Remove the breadcrumb trail from the shared layout and keep the back link, which is what DR1 shows on every page and what the GOV.UK Design System asks for: its breadcrumbs guidance says not to use breadcrumbs and a back link on the same page. Doing this removes the frontend's only standing route back to the notification list, so it should land with the service-navigation menu, whose Dashboard item is DR1's route back. If the trail is kept instead, the empty one on the dashboard has to go regardless — an empty navigation landmark is a defect on its own terms and needs no design decision.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding breadcrumbs on any DR1 screen, or any reference to the breadcrumbs component in the prototype's views.
finding.verification: Re-counted from the rendered DOM on both sides, opened the fe-declaration and dr1-declaration full-page shots, and read layout.njk:40-52 and declaration.html:13-25. All three counts hold: `govuk-breadcrumbs` is in 37 of the 40 frontend DOMs and the three that lack it are exactly fe-hub, fe-hub-no-commodity and fe-hub-exit-details-blocked; `govuk-back-link` is in 37 and the three that lack it are fe-confirmation and the two dashboards, so the two sets are disjoint and 34 screens carry both. fe-dashboard-populated renders `<nav class="govuk-breadcrumbs" aria-label="Breadcrumb">` wrapping a `govuk-breadcrumbs__list` with no list items, so the empty-landmark claim is literal. Ran the falsifier: `grep -l breadcrumb` over all 42 prototype DOMs and over the whole prototype views tree returns nothing, so it does not fire. CORRECT.

relatedTo.why: The menu's Dashboard item is what replaces the breadcrumb as the route back to the notification list.
